Committor probabilities

Source: R/probabilistic.R
committorAB.Rd

Probability that a Markov chain hits the set of states A before the set B (the committor function), from every initial state or from one.

Usage

committorAB(object, A, B, p = 1)

Arguments

object

A markovchain object.

A, B

Disjoint sets of states, given as indices (positions in states(object)).

p

Optional index of the initial state. If omitted, the probabilities for all initial states are returned.

Value

A numeric vector with the probability for each initial state, or a single number if p is given.

Details

The committor \(q\) solves the linear system \(q_i = \sum_j P_{ij} q_j\) for the states outside \(A \cup B\), with \(q = 1\) on A and \(q = 0\) on B. The system has a unique solution when A or B can be reached from every state.

See also

Other first passage and hitting: absorptionProbabilities(), firstPassage(), firstPassageMultiple(), hittingProbabilities(), meanAbsorptionTime(), meanFirstPassageTime(), meanNumVisits(), meanRecurrenceTime(), noofVisitsDist()

Examples

transMatr <- matrix(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0.5,
                      0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0,
                      0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0,
                      0, 0.2, 0.4, 0, 0,
                      0, 0.8, 0.6, 0, 0.5), nrow = 5)
object <- new("markovchain", states = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"),
              transitionMatrix = transMatr)
# probability of reaching "e" before "c", from each state
committorAB(object, 5, 3)
#>         a         b         c         d         e 
#> 0.4444444 0.8888889 0.0000000 0.4444444 1.0000000 
committorAB(object, 5, 3, p = 1)
#>         a 
#> 0.4444444
